interest: John W. Masland's 1943 memos recognized Japan's claims to the Kuriles and Southern Sakhalin, warning against Soviet transfer.
overview: This file consists of two secret research and policy memoranda prepared on May 24, 1943, by the Division of Political Studies of the U.S. Department of State (drafted by John W. Masland), designated T 322 and T-321. The documents provide comprehensive geopolitical, demographic, historical, economic, and strategic military surveys of the Kurile Islands (Chishima) and Southern Sakhalin (Japanese Karafuto) in anticipation of postwar territorial adjustments in the Far East. Both studies analyze the degree of Japanese administrative and economic integration, detail vital natural resources (especially fisheries, timber, pulp, paper, and coal), examine military and naval installations screening Siberia and the Sea of Okhotsk, and weigh alternative postwar settlements—ranging from full cession to the Soviet Union, international administration or inspection, to complete or conditional retention by Japan.

subfiles.about: A State Department policy memorandum analyzing the Kurile Islands' geography, population, administration, economic resources, strategic military position, and alternative postwar dispositions.
subfiles.from: Division of Political Studies, Department of State (John W. Masland)
subfiles.summary: This secret memorandum (T 322) analyzes the status and future disposition of the 47 islands in the Kurile chain (Chishima). It reviews the history of Japanese title established under the 1875 convention with Russia, civil administration under the Nemuro branch of Hokkaido, and the crucial economic role of Kurile fisheries, canning, and marine products. The paper details Japanese military, naval, and seaplane bases on islands such as Paramushiro, Shimushu, Shimushiri, and Etorofu, emphasizing how the chain screens Siberia and northern Japan. It concludes by evaluating five postwar options: transfer to Russia, international administration, partial retention by Japan (depriving Japan of the northernmost islands Shimushu and Paramushiro), unconditional retention by Japan, and conditional retention with total demilitarization and periodic international inspection.
subfiles.title: The Kurile Islands (Chishima) (Memorandum T 322)

subfiles.about: A State Department policy memorandum evaluating the historical claims, civil administration, economic development, strategic security value, and postwar disposition of Southern Sakhalin (Karafuto).
subfiles.from: Division of Political Studies, Department of State (John W. Masland)
subfiles.summary: This secret memorandum (T-321) examines the background, economy, and postwar status of Japanese Karafuto (Southern Sakhalin south of the 50th parallel). It outlines the historical treaties governing Sakhalin, including the 1875 exchange treaty and the 1905 Treaty of Portsmouth, and explains Karafuto's integration into Japan proper under the Ministry of Home Affairs with an overwhelmingly Japanese population. The study highlights Karafuto's significant industrial output in coal, timber, pulp, paper, and fisheries, as well as Japanese oil concessions in Soviet northern Sakhalin established after the Nikolaevsk incident. After detailing naval and air installations along La Pérouse Strait, the paper assesses three postwar solutions: transferring the territory to Russia, unconditional retention by Japan, or conditional retention subject to the dismantling of military installations and international inspection.
subfiles.title: Southern Sakhalin: Japanese Karafuto (Memorandum T-321)
